Quantity Distribution and Performance-Based Allocation i) Broad Quantity Distribution Pattern Subject to the terms and conditions of the tender, the broad quantity distribu tion pattern for splitting the order among up to eight successful bidders who match the R-1/RA-L1/negotiated final price shall be as follows: Distribution of quantity among Ratio (%) Two vendors (R-1 and R-2) 70 : 30 Three vendors (R-1 to R-3) 45 : 30 : 25 Four vendors (R-1 to R-4) 40 : 25 : 20 : 15 Five vendors (R-1 to R-5) 40 : 20 : 15 : 15 : 10 Six vendors (R-1 to R-6) 35 : 20 : 15 : 10 : 10 : 10 Seven vendors (R-1 to R-7) 35 : 20 : 15 : 8 : 8 : 7 : 7 Eight vendors (R-1 to R-8) 35 : 20 : 10 : 10 : 7 : 6 : 6 : 6 The allocation determined in accordance with the above table shall constitut e the primary allocation for applying the performance-based restriction sp ecified below. ii) Performance-Based Restriction on Primary Allocation While allocating quantity to a successful bidder, the bidder’s past delivery pe rformance against the latest Purchase Order(s) issued by RCF shall also be ta ken into consideration. The delivery-performance percentage shall be calculated with reference to t he completed delivery schedules under such Purchase Order(s). For each co mpleted delivery schedule, only the quantity actually supplied within the stip ulated delivery period shall be considered. Where the quantity supplied against a particular delivery schedule exceeds t

he quantity allotted under that schedule, the quantity considered for perfor mance calculation shall be restricted to the quantity allotted under that deliv ery schedule. Excess quantity supplied against one delivery schedule shall n ot be adjusted against any shortfall under another delivery schedule. The delivery performance shall be calculated as follows: Delivery Performance (%) = (Total eligible quantity supplied within the stipulated delivery period against completed delivery schedules ÷ Total quantity allotted under such completed delivery schedules) × 100 The quantity otherwise eligible for allocation to the bidder under the present tender, in accordance with the NIT conditions and the applicable Broad Quan tity Distribution Pattern, shall be restricted proportionately to the bidder’s de livery-performance percentage. Accordingly: Performance-Adjusted Quantity = Primary Allocation under the NIT × Delivery Performance (%) iii) Illustration of Performance-Based Allocation Under the earlier contract, the vendor was allotted delivery schedules of 10 l akh bags each for the months of January, February, March, April, May and June, aggregating to 60 lakh bags. The supplies made against these d elivery schedules were as follows: Eligible quantity Delivery sc Quantity al Quantity su considered for perform hedule lotted pplied ance January 10 lakh 7 lakh 7 lakh February 10 lakh 12 lakh 10 lakh March 10 lakh 11 lakh 10 lakh April 10 lakh 6 lakh 6 lakh May 10 lakh 8 lakh 8 lakh June 10 lakh 10 lakh 10 lakh Total 60 lakh 54 lakh 51 lakh Although the vendor supplied 12 lakh bags against the February delivery sc hedule and 11 lakh bags against the March delivery schedule, the eligible q uantity for each of these schedules shall be restricted to the scheduled quan

tity of 10 lakh bags. The excess quantities supplied against these schedule s shall not compensate for shortfalls under other delivery schedules. Any balance quantity supplied during July or thereafter shall not be consid ered for performance calculation against the above completed delivery sche dules if such quantity is supplied beyond their respective stipulated delivery periods. Accordingly: · Total quantity allotted under the completed delivery schedule s: 60 lakh bags · Total eligible quantity supplied within the stipulated delivery periods: 51 lakh bags Therefore: Delivery Performance = (51 ÷ 60) × 100 = 85% If the vendor is otherwise entitled to a primary allocation of 72 lakh bags un der the present tender as per the NIT conditions, the quantity allocable after considering its past delivery performance shall be: Performance-Adjusted Quantity = 85% of 72 lakh bags = 61.20 lakh bags Accordingly, the vendor’s allocation under the present tender shall be restric ted to 61.20 lakh bags, subject further to the MSE-allocation provisions, th e quantity offered by the bidder and the ceiling of 40% of its annual producti on capacity. iv) Allocation to MSE Bidders After determining the primary allocation and applying the performance-base d restriction: a. If the aggregate quantity allotted to all MSE bidders qualifying in accordan ce with Annexure VI is equal to or more than 25% of the total order quant ity, the distribution shall remain unaltered. b. If the aggregate quantity allotted to all such eligible MSE bidders is less th an 25% of the total order quantity, the quantity allotted to the MSE bidders shall be enhanced on a pro-rata basis by correspondingly reducing th e quantities allotted to non-MSE bidders, so as to allocate 25% of the total order quantity to eligible MSE bidders. c. The quantity finally awarded to any bidder, including an MSE bidder, shall not exceed the lower of: · the quantity offered by the bidder; or · 40% of the bidder’s annual production capacity. d. If any portion of the 25% quantity earmarked for eligible MSE bidders rem ains unallocated after applying the above limitations, the unallocated quantit y shall be redistributed among the eligible non-MSE bidders who have match

ed the R-1/RA-L1/negotiated final price, subject to the applicable distribution ratio, performance-based restriction, offered quantity and annual-production -capacity ceiling. v) Tentative Distribution Ratio for Non-MSE Bidders Where 25% of the total order quantity is allocated to eligible MSE bidders, th e tentative distribution ratio for non-MSE bidders in respect of the balance 75 % of the order quantity shall be as follows: Total number of ven Ratio for non-MSE bidders (% of total order q dors uantity) Two vendors 75 Three vendors 42 : 33 Four vendors 33 : 23 : 19 Five vendors 33 : 19 : 14 : 9 Six vendors 33 : 19 : 9 : 7 : 7 Seven vendors 33 : 16 : 9 : 7 : 5 : 5 Eight vendors 33 : 15 : 9 : 5 : 5 : 4 : 4 vi) Redistribution of Unallocated Quantity If the quantity offered by any bidder is lower than the quantity otherwise allo cable to that bidder under the applicable Broad Quantity Distribution Pattern, the resultant unallocated quantity shall be redistributed among the remainin g eligible bidders who: · have matched the R-1/RA-L1/negotiated final price; and · have offered a quantity higher than their respective allocable quantiti es. Such redistribution shall, as far as practicable, be carried out in accordance with the applicable relative ratios under the Broad Quantity Distribution Patt ern. Any quantity becoming available on account of the performance-based restri ction applicable to a bidder may also be redistributed among the other eligibl e bidders who have matched the R-1/RA-L1/negotiated final price, subject to their respective delivery performance, offered quantities, annual production capacities and the applicable MSE-allocation provisions. As a result of such restriction or redistribution, the final allocation may differ from the Broad Quantity Distribution Pattern indicated above.
